comment: (GES187) Dr. Legro is extremely passionate, which makes class engaging. The readings are very long and complex, and class time is stressful because he expects a lot of participation. He wants his students to succeed, so if you take his corrections and meet with him outside class, you will do well. If you want an easy gen ed DO NOT TAKE

(Causes of the world) Professor Legro is exceptional but difficult. I would recommend taking this course, but beware that if you are disinterested in the topics it is a lot of work. Participation matters and you cannot sneak away without doing the work. He is incredibly helpful and accessible out of class, and he KNOWS his stuff.

Legro will teach you a lot and how to think critically, but also he is very particular about the structure of papers/speeches/presentations etc. His FYS is supposedly one of the harder classes, but it is significantly more rewarding.

You are going to leave this classroom with an incredible amount of knowledge for his Causes of the World seminar. Each class you prepare with an article and make a theory journal, which is then reviewed and built on in class with small groups. He takes the time to engage with students and make sure students know each other. Tough essay grader.

Took FYS "On Strategy" in Fall 2024. I could tell Legro is really smart, but the structure of the class was not good. We had almost no work for the first two months of the class, then during the last few weeks it felt like there was a lengthy assignment due every class period. Also very harsh grader for a freshman seminar class.

Dr. Legro is an incredibly fair professor, but his grading may be perceived as difficult for an FYS or 100-level class. His class does not necessarily require a large amount of time, but he certainly forces you to think critically and will expose weaknesses in your writing, speaking, or arguments. He holds all students to a high standard.

I had Jeff in my FYS. He is extremely knowledgeable in the field of strategy and will probe you on your points in an effort to make you better. The majority of his FYS On Strategy was on US foreign policy. Jeff is challenging, but if you buy in, his class is one of the most inspiring courses you can take.
